title: Fantasy and Its Old Myths
objective: After this level you can trace how Tolkien built Middle-earth from Norse myth and Beowulf.
summary: Tolkien, an Oxford scholar of Old English, took dwarf names from the Poetic Edda and modeled Gandalf on Odin. Bilbo's stolen cup echoes Beowulf's dragon.

cards.headline: Tolkien's dwarves got their names from an Old Norse poem.
cards.body: Thorin, Durin, Bombur, Nori: the dwarves of Middle-earth sound made up. Yet their names match dwarves listed in the Völuspá, a poem of the Poetic Edda: the same poem that tells of Ragnarök in Level 12. Tolkien didn't only invent a world. He dug one up.

cards.headline: A professor of old words
cards.body: J. R. R. Tolkien taught at Oxford from 1925 to 1959, specializing in Old and Middle English, and gave a landmark 1936 lecture on Beowulf. The Hobbit followed in 1937, The Lord of the Rings in 1954 to 1955. In his letters he described a bigger ambition: to create a mythology for England. The raw material was on his desk.

cards.headline: A wizard in the shape of a god
cards.body: The names were only the start. Gandalf's likely model is Odin, the Norse king of the gods from Level 11, who in Norse poems travels among humans as a wandering wizard, coming and going with his own purposes. Sound familiar? That is Gandalf's whole job description.

cards.headline: One stolen cup
cards.body: In Beowulf (Level 47), a dragon is enraged when a man steals from its hoard; in J. Lesslie Hall's translation it misses its "gem-cup" and ravages the land with fire. In The Hobbit, Bilbo carries off a great two-handled cup from the sleeping Smaug, who wakes in fury. Copied? In a 1938 letter, Tolkien called Beowulf among his most valued sources, but said it wasn't consciously in his mind as he wrote: the theft arose naturally from the story.

learned: Dwarf names from the Poetic Edda
A stolen cup links Beowulf and The Hobbit
Tolkien: Beowulf valued, the theft natural

questions.prompt: Dwarf names like Thorin and Durin come from _____.

options.label: Beowulf's list of Danish kings
options.rationale: Beowulf gave him the stolen cup, not these names.

options.label: Ovid's Metamorphoses
options.rationale: Ovid's myths are Greek and Roman.

options.label: Tolkien's own invention
options.rationale: They match names in an Old Norse poem.

questions.explanation: Many of Tolkien's dwarf names, including Thorin and Durin, match dwarves named in the Völuspá of the Poetic Edda.

questions.prompt: Bilbo's cup theft looks a lot like Beowulf's. Which explanation matches what Tolkien himself said in 1938?

options.label: He copied the scene from Beowulf on purpose
options.rationale: He said it wasn't consciously in his mind.

options.label: He had never read Beowulf
options.rationale: He gave a landmark lecture on it in 1936.

options.label: Beowulf was a valued source, but the theft arose naturally
He took the theft from the Poetic Edda
options.rationale: He named Beowulf as the valued source.

questions.explanation: Tolkien called Beowulf among his most valued sources but said the theft arose naturally from the story, not from conscious borrowing.

questions.prompt: Level 6's singers inherited phrases and scenes and reshaped them. What did Tolkien do with the dwarf names of the Völuspá?

options.label: Translated the whole poem word for word
options.rationale: He took names, not the whole poem.

options.label: Replaced them with names in Latin
Kept them as a secret code for scholars
options.rationale: They are the names of his characters.

options.label: Reused them for the dwarves of his own story

questions.explanation: Like Homer's singers reshaping inherited material, Tolkien reused old Norse dwarf names for the dwarves of Middle-earth.
